top_news.title: India: End Crackdown on Protesters, Arbitrary Detentions
top_news.summary: Click to expand Image Police detain protesters during a demonstration demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in New Delhi, India, Saturday, October 10, 2026. 2026 AP Photo/Manish Swarup (New York) -Indian authorities are using abusive methods tocrack down on thousands of peaceful protesters in New Delhi and other Indian cities, Human Rights Watch said today. The protests, led by the Gen Z Cockroach Janta Party, opposition parties, student organizations, and civil society groups, have demanded the resignation of the country's top election official over alleged wrongdoing and the scrapping of acontentious voter list revision process. As the protests grew in October 2026, the police have beat protesters, forcibly dragged them on the streets and stuffed them into vans and buses, arbitrarily detained them, imposed excessive restrictions on movement, and suspended mobile internet services. The authorities have alsoharassed and arbitrarilydetained journalists covering the protests. "Police in Delhi are responding to peaceful protests with seemingly unnecessary or excessive force and have wrongfully detained thousands of people," saidElaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. "The Modi government should stop throwing young protesters in jail and instead engage with them to address concerns over the right to vote and fairness of elections." Prime Minister Narendra Modi's administration should stop the ill-treatment and arbitrary detention of protesters, allow people to protest peacefully, and restore mobile internet services and freedom of movement, Human Rights Watch said. Since June 2025, the Election Commission of India has carried out a nationwide Special Intensive Revision (SIR) to clean electoral rolls, ostensibly to remove any dead, duplicate, or ineligible voters. But the process, which has deleted more than 130 million names so far, has been arbitrary and opaque, prompting fears of mass disenfranchisement, and is disproportionately affecting Muslims and otherreligious minorities, women, and people living in poverty.Protest leaders andopposition parties allege that the commission hasmanipulated the lists to benefit Prime Minister Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The protests began on September 25, soon after the Indian Express published its investigation into alleged irregularities in the revision process. The newspaper found that the Election Commission's two commissioners had raised multiple objections against decisions by the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar. Petitionschallenging the revision process and seeking Kumar's removal are before the Supreme Court. As protests inDelhi grew in October, security forces arbitrarily arrested and assaulted numerous protesters each day, and took them to undisclosed locations, later releasing many of them. Those detained included journalists and political opposition leaders, includingfour former chief ministers andRahul Gandhi, the leader of the opposition. When the protests began, Delhi Police released a set of "guidelines," instructing journalists to "carry valid identity cards" that are "visibly displayed," to "not obstruct police operations," and to "maintain a reasonable and safe distance." On October 11, theSupreme Court directed that lawyers and journalists "should not be impeded from carrying out their professional duties." On October 10 and 11, officials arbitrarily detained at least30 journalists who were covering the protests. Four journalists' organizationscondemned the police actions, saying that journalists were "bundled into buses" used to detain protesters, and that police seized some of their phones and equipment. Three female journalists alleged that Delhi police officers sexually harassed them during the protests. A journalist from the magazineCaravan said that on October 11,police officers in Delhi hit him on the head several times, slapped him, and assaulted him with a rifle butt while he recorded them detaining a protester. "My press card was hanging by my neck but they still dragged me into the bus, ripping my shirt buttons," a 31-year-old journalist told Human Rights Watch. Police detained him in a bus on October 10, and he was released only after the bus overheated and caught fire. "We could smell the fumes and had to shout at them to get us out," he said. "The police personnel assaulted me and pinned me to the seat," saidJohn Brittas, a member of parliament participating in the protests, ina letter to the chief justice of India. The Cockroach Janta Party called for a protest on October 10 at Jantar Mantar, a designated protest site in Delhi. In response the authorities deployed over40,000 security forces,canceled trains, shut down43 metro stations, and suspendedmobile internet services. Police tookthree Cockroach Janta Party leaders into custody aboard an airplane after it landed in Delhi, dragged several protesters from trains and buses who were traveling to Delhi, and putsome youth leaders under house arrest. Air India has sought a response from the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security on how security forces entered its aircraft without prior authorization. On October 9, a police officer entered a Delhi mosque during Friday prayers to warn Muslims against participating in any "unnecessary protests." The next day, police officialsentered a Sikh temple in central Delhi to detain protesters who sought refuge there. Citizens for Fraternity-Bharat (CFF-Bharat), acivil society group that includes former government officials, has questioned why police entered religious premises and called for an independent inquiry. On October 11, India's Supreme Courtdirected the authorities to ensure that people gathering peacefully are not illegally detained, internet services are restored, andpeople and traffic are allowed to move freely, subject to lawful restrictions. Thus far, the authorities appear to have ignored the directions. A journalist, 26, told Human Rights Watch he witnessed at least three instances in which BJP supporters and police chased protesters together. "It is collaborative," said the journalist, who covered the protests on October 10. "The police looked on and did not stop the violence." A female journalist, 27, said a group of about five men, some of them wearing saffron scarves, were beating protesters and targeting female journalists. "They were shouting at us, mocking us, and showing us the middle finger," she said. "I saw two policemen laughing while the right-wing goons were kicking and beating protesters." The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights expressed concerns over the mass detention of demonstrators and said that the government should engage in meaningful dialogue. The Indian Ministry of External Affairscalled the statement "unwarranted" and "an unacceptable interference in the internal affairs of India." The Indian government should publicly direct security forces to respond to protests in accordance with international standards, notably the UN Basic Principles on the Use of Force and Firearms by Law Enforcement Officials, Human Rights Watch said. "Indian authorities should allow people to protest peacefully by resuming transport services, removing unnecessary barricades, restoring the internet, and ensuring media freedom," Pearson said. "Peaceful protest and freedom of expression are fundamental rights protected under the international human rights law that India's leaders claim to uphold."

top_news.title: "Punjab gov is being run by drug mafia": Manjinder Singh Sirsa blames AAP govt for anti-drug activist's murder
top_news.summary: Delhi Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Tuesday launched a scathing attack on the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab, alleging a direct nexus between the administration and the "drug mafia" following the murder of Anti-drug activist Parminder Singh Jhota in Mansa. Addressing the reporters, Sirsa claimed that the incident highlights a state of lawlessness similar to cartel-run nations. "A very major incident occurred just a short while ago. As we have been saying repeatedly, the Punjab government is being run by a drug mafia. It seems that Bhagwant Mann, Arvind Kejriwal, and Manish Sisodia are taking a lot of money from the drug mafia," Sirsa alleged. Drawing a grim comparison, Sirsa argued that Punjab is witnessing an unprecedented decline in public safety for those challenging the illicit narcotics trade. "Today, a Mansa-based drug activist-whom the Punjab police had previously arrested and tortured just because he spoke out against drugs-has now been murdered," he stated. "Just imagine, this kind of thing used to happen in America or Colombia, where those who spoke out against drugs were killed. Today, Punjab has become the same kind of state, where the police either torture people and put them in jail, or, as in today's incident, someone who was fighting against drugs was murdered. This shows the state of drug issues in Punjab," he added. Sirsa's remarks come after Jhota, who was known for his activism against drugs in Mansa, was shot by a medical shop owner. He was taken to a hospital after sustaining bullet injuries and later succumbed to them. The killing of Jhota has ignited a political firestorm with opposition leaders tearing into the Bhagwant Mann-led government alleging a failure of law and order and questioning the effectiveness of the state's campaign against drugs. Former Punjab Congress president Raja Warring, in a post on X said, "The daylight murder of Parminder Singh Jhota is a direct result of the failed law & order and failed 'Yudh Nashean Virudh' of the @BhagwantMann govt. Parminder stood up against Punjab's drug menace but his initiatives were never supported by the @AAPPunjab govt. His broad daylight murder exposes Serious failures of the AAP Govt." Congress leader Sukhpal Singh Khaira also targeted the AAP government, alleging that the killing exposed the failure of its anti-drug campaign. "The broad daylight murder of Parminder Singh Jhota a known and drug activist of Punjab only shows how powerful #DrugMafia is under the @AamAadmiParty govt! Treatment involves medical detoxification and other clinical interventions in order to bring back the brain's balance, which makes it responsive again to natural reinforcers. top_news.title: Noida
top_news.summary: Aadinath Ur Homes, a Noida-based real estate consultancy and advisory firm with more than two decades of experience in the region, led by CEO & Director Gaurav Jain, said Noida's commercial real estate market is entering a new phase of growth, supported by infrastructure expansion, improving regional connectivity, rising corporate demand and the commencement of commercial flight operations at Noida International Airport in June 2026. The operationalisation of Noida International Airport, along with continued infrastructure development across the Noida-Greater Noida and Yamuna Expressway corridors, is adding a new dimension to the region's commercial growth outlook. This comes amid sustained momentum in India's office market. According to CBRE's India Office Figures Q3 2026, India's office sector recorded approximately 21.0 million sq. ft. of absorption in Q3 2026, taking January-September absorption to a record 66.4 million sq. ft., up 8% year-on-year. Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru and Hyderabad together accounted for 69% of quarterly leasing activity. Infrastructure and connectivity reshape Noida's commercial landscape Connectivity is becoming an increasingly important consideration for businesses evaluating office and commercial locations. Noida benefits from established road infrastructure, metro connectivity and links with Delhi, Greater Noida and other NCR markets. The Noida-Greater Noida Expressway and Yamuna Expressway have supported the development of new commercial, institutional, residential and logistics corridors. The infrastructure-led expansion is also contributing to the emergence of newer commercial locations beyond Noida's traditional business districts. As development extends towards Greater Noida and the Yamuna Expressway corridor, businesses and investors are increasingly evaluating locations based on accessibility, workplace quality, proximity to residential catchments, supporting infrastructure and long-term development potential. The growth of commercial infrastructure is also supporting the emergence of new business hubs across Noida and the wider region. Areas along major expressways and established commercial corridors are attracting office developments, retail destinations, hospitality projects and mixed-use developments, creating broader ecosystems for businesses and consumers. Noida International Airport strengthens regional connectivity A major milestone for the region in 2026 has been the commencement of commercial operations at Noida International Airport. Noida International Airport commenced commercial flight operations on June 15, 2026, with IndiGo operating the first commercial flight. The airport had earlier received its aerodrome licence from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation. The first phase of the airport has been designed to serve 12 million passengers annually, while the master plan provides for phased expansion to more than 70 million passengers annually. The airport is also developing an integrated cargo and logistics ecosystem. Its cargo facilities have an initial handling capacity of 200,000 metric tonnes annually, with plans to scale capacity substantially. The cargo infrastructure is designed to support e-commerce, freight forwarding and logistics activity across North India. The airport's operationalisation adds another layer to the economic infrastructure of Noida, Greater Noida and the Yamuna Expressway region, with potential implications for aviation-linked businesses, logistics, hospitality, retail and commercial development. The development is also expected to strengthen the broader regional ecosystem by improving access to domestic and international markets and supporting the growth of allied commercial activity. Corporate expansion continues to support office demand The broader Indian office market is also being supported by expansion from domestic and global occupiers. CBRE reported that Global Capability Centres accounted for approximately 41% of India's office space take-up in Q3 2026, while GCC leasing during the first nine months of 2026 reached a record approximately 28 million sq. ft. Flexible workspace operators accounted for 24% of Q3 leasing, followed by BFSI companies at 22% and technology companies at 15%. Independent research from Colliers also points to continued strength in Delhi-NCR. The region recorded 8.3 million sq. ft. of Grade A office leasing during January-September 2026, representing a 17% year-on-year increase, while Q3 leasing reached 3.3 million sq. ft. For Noida, these broader trends are relevant as the city continues to attract technology companies, financial services firms, startups, healthcare organisations, educational institutions, multinational corporations and professional services businesses. The resulting commercial ecosystem is increasingly diversified, spanning office spaces, retail destinations, mixed-use developments, serviced apartments and other business-oriented formats. For businesses, access to quality commercial spaces, connectivity to residential catchments and proximity to major transportation networks are becoming increasingly important factors in location decisions. This is supporting demand across strategically located commercial micro-markets. Aadinath Ur Homes' commercial market presence Aadinath Ur Homes has advisory and sales involvement across a range of commercial developments in Noida and Greater Noida, including Bhutani Cyberthum in Sector 140A, Noida; Bhutani Astrathum in Greater Noida West; Bhutani City Centre 32 in Sector 32, Noida; and Spectrum Metro in Sector 75, Noida. These developments represent a mix of office spaces, retail destinations, mixed-use SOHO formats and serviced apartments, reflecting the changing nature of commercial real estate demand across Noida and the wider NCR market. From an advisory perspective, commercial opportunities are evaluated on factors including location, connectivity, project status, developer credentials, surrounding development, market demand and leasing potential. Evolving commercial corridors create new opportunities Noida's commercial growth is increasingly extending beyond its established business districts. Infrastructure-led development along major expressways and connecting corridors is creating opportunities for new office, retail, hospitality and mixed-use destinations. From an investment perspective, infrastructure can play an important role in shaping the long-term potential of a real estate market. Improved connectivity, employment generation, commercial activity and supporting social infrastructure can collectively influence the attractiveness of emerging locations. The increasing integration of commercial developments with retail, hospitality, entertainment and lifestyle offerings is also creating more comprehensive business destinations rather than standalone office or retail clusters. As businesses continue to evaluate locations based on connectivity, accessibility and operational efficiency, commercial corridors with strong infrastructure linkages are likely to remain areas of interest. Looking ahead Noida's next phase of commercial growth is being shaped by the convergence of infrastructure development, corporate expansion and regional connectivity. The operationalisation of Noida International Airport represents a significant addition to the region's infrastructure network, while its developing passenger and cargo ecosystem could support further economic activity across Noida, Greater Noida and the Yamuna Expressway corridor. At the same time, the latest 2026 data from CBRE and Colliers points to continued demand for quality office space across India and Delhi-NCR. The record 66.4 million sq. ft. of office absorption across India during January-September 2026 and 8.3 million sq. ft. of Grade A leasing in Delhi-NCR during the same period reflect continued occupier activity. For investors and occupiers, the evolving market reinforces the importance of evaluating individual projects on fundamentals rather than relying solely on broader market trends. Factors such as location, connectivity, surrounding development, tenant or consumer demand, developer credentials, project status and the potential evolution of the micro-market remain important considerations. With infrastructure, connectivity and business activity continuing to develop, Noida is positioned to remain an important commercial destination within the wider Delhi-NCR economic ecosystem. articles.title: India: End Crackdown on Protesters, Arbitrary Detentions
articles.summary: Click to expand Image Police detain protesters during a demonstration demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar in New Delhi, India, Saturday, October 10, 2026. 2026 AP Photo/Manish Swarup (New York) -Indian authorities are using abusive methods tocrack down on thousands of peaceful protesters in New Delhi and other Indian cities, Human Rights Watch said today. The protests, led by the Gen Z Cockroach Janta Party, opposition parties, student organizations, and civil society groups, have demanded the resignation of the country's top election official over alleged wrongdoing and the scrapping of acontentious voter list revision process. As the protests grew in October 2026, the police have beat protesters, forcibly dragged them on the streets and stuffed them into vans and buses, arbitrarily detained them, imposed excessive restrictions on movement, and suspended mobile internet services. The authorities have alsoharassed and arbitrarilydetained journalists covering the protests. "Police in Delhi are responding to peaceful protests with seemingly unnecessary or excessive force and have wrongfully detained thousands of people," saidElaine Pearson, Asia director at Human Rights Watch. "The Modi government should stop throwing young protesters in jail and instead engage with them to address concerns over the right to vote and fairness of elections." Prime Minister Narendra Modi's administration should stop the ill-treatment and arbitrary detention of protesters, allow people to protest peacefully, and restore mobile internet services and freedom of movement, Human Rights Watch said. Since June 2025, the Election Commission of India has carried out a nationwide Special Intensive Revision (SIR) to clean electoral rolls, ostensibly to remove any dead, duplicate, or ineligible voters. But the process, which has deleted more than 130 million names so far, has been arbitrary and opaque, prompting fears of mass disenfranchisement, and is disproportionately affecting Muslims and otherreligious minorities, women, and people living in poverty.Protest leaders andopposition parties allege that the commission hasmanipulated the lists to benefit Prime Minister Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The protests began on September 25, soon after the Indian Express published its investigation into alleged irregularities in the revision process. The newspaper found that the Election Commission's two commissioners had raised multiple objections against decisions by the chief election commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar. Petitionschallenging the revision process and seeking Kumar's removal are before the Supreme Court. As protests inDelhi grew in October, security forces arbitrarily arrested and assaulted numerous protesters each day, and took them to undisclosed locations, later releasing many of them. Those detained included journalists and political opposition leaders, includingfour former chief ministers andRahul Gandhi, the leader of the opposition. When the protests began, Delhi Police released a set of "guidelines," instructing journalists to "carry valid identity cards" that are "visibly displayed," to "not obstruct police operations," and to "maintain a reasonable and safe distance." On October 11, theSupreme Court directed that lawyers and journalists "should not be impeded from carrying out their professional duties." On October 10 and 11, officials arbitrarily detained at least30 journalists who were covering the protests. Four journalists' organizationscondemned the police actions, saying that journalists were "bundled into buses" used to detain protesters, and that police seized some of their phones and equipment. Three female journalists alleged that Delhi police officers sexually harassed them during the protests. A journalist from the magazineCaravan said that on October 11,police officers in Delhi hit him on the head several times, slapped him, and assaulted him with a rifle butt while he recorded them detaining a protester. "My press card was hanging by my neck but they still dragged me into the bus, ripping my shirt buttons," a 31-year-old journalist told Human Rights Watch. Police detained him in a bus on October 10, and he was released only after the bus overheated and caught fire. "We could smell the fumes and had to shout at them to get us out," he said. "The police personnel assaulted me and pinned me to the seat," saidJohn Brittas, a member of parliament participating in the protests, ina letter to the chief justice of India. The Cockroach Janta Party called for a protest on October 10 at Jantar Mantar, a designated protest site in Delhi. In response the authorities deployed over40,000 security forces,canceled trains, shut down43 metro stations, and suspendedmobile internet services. Police tookthree Cockroach Janta Party leaders into custody aboard an airplane after it landed in Delhi, dragged several protesters from trains and buses who were traveling to Delhi, and putsome youth leaders under house arrest. Air India has sought a response from the Bureau of Civil Aviation Security on how security forces entered its aircraft without prior authorization. On October 9, a police officer entered a Delhi mosque during Friday prayers to warn Muslims against participating in any "unnecessary protests." The next day, police officialsentered a Sikh temple in central Delhi to detain protesters who sought refuge there. Citizens for Fraternity-Bharat (CFF-Bharat), acivil society group that includes former government officials, has questioned why police entered religious premises and called for an independent inquiry. On October 11, India's Supreme Courtdirected the authorities to ensure that people gathering peacefully are not illegally detained, internet services are restored, andpeople and traffic are allowed to move freely, subject to lawful restrictions. Thus far, the authorities appear to have ignored the directions. A journalist, 26, told Human Rights Watch he witnessed at least three instances in which BJP supporters and police chased protesters together. "It is collaborative," said the journalist, who covered the protests on October 10. "The police looked on and did not stop the violence." A female journalist, 27, said a group of about five men, some of them wearing saffron scarves, were beating protesters and targeting female journalists. "They were shouting at us, mocking us, and showing us the middle finger," she said. "I saw two policemen laughing while the right-wing goons were kicking and beating protesters." The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights expressed concerns over the mass detention of demonstrators and said that the government should engage in meaningful dialogue. The Indian Ministry of External Affairscalled the statement "unwarranted" and "an unacceptable interference in the internal affairs of India." The Indian government should publicly direct security forces to respond to protests in accordance with international standards, notably the UN Basic Principles on the Use of Force and Firearms by Law Enforcement Officials, Human Rights Watch said. "Indian authorities should allow people to protest peacefully by resuming transport services, removing unnecessary barricades, restoring the internet, and ensuring media freedom," Pearson said. "Peaceful protest and freedom of expression are fundamental rights protected under the international human rights law that India's leaders claim to uphold."

articles.title: "Punjab gov is being run by drug mafia": Manjinder Singh Sirsa blames AAP govt for anti-drug activist's murder
articles.summary: Delhi Minister Manjinder Singh Sirsa on Tuesday launched a scathing attack on the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) government in Punjab, alleging a direct nexus between the administration and the "drug mafia" following the murder of Anti-drug activist Parminder Singh Jhota in Mansa. Addressing the reporters, Sirsa claimed that the incident highlights a state of lawlessness similar to cartel-run nations. "A very major incident occurred just a short while ago. As we have been saying repeatedly, the Punjab government is being run by a drug mafia. It seems that Bhagwant Mann, Arvind Kejriwal, and Manish Sisodia are taking a lot of money from the drug mafia," Sirsa alleged. Drawing a grim comparison, Sirsa argued that Punjab is witnessing an unprecedented decline in public safety for those challenging the illicit narcotics trade. "Today, a Mansa-based drug activist-whom the Punjab police had previously arrested and tortured just because he spoke out against drugs-has now been murdered," he stated. "Just imagine, this kind of thing used to happen in America or Colombia, where those who spoke out against drugs were killed. Today, Punjab has become the same kind of state, where the police either torture people and put them in jail, or, as in today's incident, someone who was fighting against drugs was murdered. This shows the state of drug issues in Punjab," he added. Sirsa's remarks come after Jhota, who was known for his activism against drugs in Mansa, was shot by a medical shop owner. He was taken to a hospital after sustaining bullet injuries and later succumbed to them. The killing of Jhota has ignited a political firestorm with opposition leaders tearing into the Bhagwant Mann-led government alleging a failure of law and order and questioning the effectiveness of the state's campaign against drugs. Former Punjab Congress president Raja Warring, in a post on X said, "The daylight murder of Parminder Singh Jhota is a direct result of the failed law & order and failed 'Yudh Nashean Virudh' of the @BhagwantMann govt. Parminder stood up against Punjab's drug menace but his initiatives were never supported by the @AAPPunjab govt. His broad daylight murder exposes Serious failures of the AAP Govt." Congress leader Sukhpal Singh Khaira also targeted the AAP government, alleging that the killing exposed the failure of its anti-drug campaign. "The broad daylight murder of Parminder Singh Jhota a known and drug activist of Punjab only shows how powerful #DrugMafia is under the @AamAadmiParty govt! Politician-Police-Drug Mafia nexus rules the roost in Punjab," Khaira said in a post on X. Shiromani Akali Dal leader Bikram Singh Majithia alleged that Jhota was shot while recording drug dealers on camera. "Parvinder Jhotta, who was fighting against the drug menace in Mansa, was shot at and subsequently died," Majithia said. Sukhbir Badal, President of the Shiromani Akali DaI also slammed the state government accusing them of criminal negligence. "I am profoundly shocked to learn about the merciless killing of Parvinder Singh Jhota by a drug trafficker. This heinous murder is a stark reminder that law and order has ceased to exist in Punjab. The deceased had been continuously raising his voice against the drug menace but no one took heed and no one supported him. The much-hyped Yudh Nashian Virudh is nothing but a gimmick and has completely failed. Recent events have exposed how the Guru-Dokhi Bhagwant Mann led AAP dispensation is completely engrossed in looting Punjab and draining the state's resources to enrich itself. They have zero attention towards the fast deteriorating situation in the state, and it is because of this criminal negligence that Punjabis are suffering every single day. This jungle raj must end," he asserted. (ANI)

articles.summary: De-addiction treatment works by reversing and rewiring the neural damage caused by Substance Use Disorder (SUD). SUD is seen as a chronic brain disorder and not a failure in one's moral values and willpower. This is due to the reason that the brain is structurally changed through chronic substance use and its effects on the mesolimbic dopamine pathway, the reward circuitry, which involves reward, motivation, and learning. Treatment involves medical detoxification and other clinical interventions in order to bring back the brain's balance, which makes it responsive again to natural reinforcers. The process of recovery becomes comprehensible. But only when it is viewed through a lens of clinical intervention, not a criminal process. articles.title: Noida
articles.summary: Aadinath Ur Homes, a Noida-based real estate consultancy and advisory firm with more than two decades of experience in the region, led by CEO & Director Gaurav Jain, said Noida's commercial real estate market is entering a new phase of growth, supported by infrastructure expansion, improving regional connectivity, rising corporate demand and the commencement of commercial flight operations at Noida International Airport in June 2026. The operationalisation of Noida International Airport, along with continued infrastructure development across the Noida-Greater Noida and Yamuna Expressway corridors, is adding a new dimension to the region's commercial growth outlook. This comes amid sustained momentum in India's office market. According to CBRE's India Office Figures Q3 2026, India's office sector recorded approximately 21.0 million sq. ft. of absorption in Q3 2026, taking January-September absorption to a record 66.4 million sq. ft., up 8% year-on-year. Delhi-NCR, Bengaluru and Hyderabad together accounted for 69% of quarterly leasing activity. Infrastructure and connectivity reshape Noida's commercial landscape Connectivity is becoming an increasingly important consideration for businesses evaluating office and commercial locations. Noida benefits from established road infrastructure, metro connectivity and links with Delhi, Greater Noida and other NCR markets. The Noida-Greater Noida Expressway and Yamuna Expressway have supported the development of new commercial, institutional, residential and logistics corridors. The infrastructure-led expansion is also contributing to the emergence of newer commercial locations beyond Noida's traditional business districts. As development extends towards Greater Noida and the Yamuna Expressway corridor, businesses and investors are increasingly evaluating locations based on accessibility, workplace quality, proximity to residential catchments, supporting infrastructure and long-term development potential. The growth of commercial infrastructure is also supporting the emergence of new business hubs across Noida and the wider region. Areas along major expressways and established commercial corridors are attracting office developments, retail destinations, hospitality projects and mixed-use developments, creating broader ecosystems for businesses and consumers. Noida International Airport strengthens regional connectivity A major milestone for the region in 2026 has been the commencement of commercial operations at Noida International Airport. Noida International Airport commenced commercial flight operations on June 15, 2026, with IndiGo operating the first commercial flight. The airport had earlier received its aerodrome licence from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation. The first phase of the airport has been designed to serve 12 million passengers annually, while the master plan provides for phased expansion to more than 70 million passengers annually. The airport is also developing an integrated cargo and logistics ecosystem. Its cargo facilities have an initial handling capacity of 200,000 metric tonnes annually, with plans to scale capacity substantially. The cargo infrastructure is designed to support e-commerce, freight forwarding and logistics activity across North India. The airport's operationalisation adds another layer to the economic infrastructure of Noida, Greater Noida and the Yamuna Expressway region, with potential implications for aviation-linked businesses, logistics, hospitality, retail and commercial development. The development is also expected to strengthen the broader regional ecosystem by improving access to domestic and international markets and supporting the growth of allied commercial activity. Corporate expansion continues to support office demand The broader Indian office market is also being supported by expansion from domestic and global occupiers. CBRE reported that Global Capability Centres accounted for approximately 41% of India's office space take-up in Q3 2026, while GCC leasing during the first nine months of 2026 reached a record approximately 28 million sq. ft. Flexible workspace operators accounted for 24% of Q3 leasing, followed by BFSI companies at 22% and technology companies at 15%. Independent research from Colliers also points to continued strength in Delhi-NCR. The region recorded 8.3 million sq. ft. of Grade A office leasing during January-September 2026, representing a 17% year-on-year increase, while Q3 leasing reached 3.3 million sq. ft. For Noida, these broader trends are relevant as the city continues to attract technology companies, financial services firms, startups, healthcare organisations, educational institutions, multinational corporations and professional services businesses. The resulting commercial ecosystem is increasingly diversified, spanning office spaces, retail destinations, mixed-use developments, serviced apartments and other business-oriented formats. For businesses, access to quality commercial spaces, connectivity to residential catchments and proximity to major transportation networks are becoming increasingly important factors in location decisions. This is supporting demand across strategically located commercial micro-markets. Aadinath Ur Homes' commercial market presence Aadinath Ur Homes has advisory and sales involvement across a range of commercial developments in Noida and Greater Noida, including Bhutani Cyberthum in Sector 140A, Noida; Bhutani Astrathum in Greater Noida West; Bhutani City Centre 32 in Sector 32, Noida; and Spectrum Metro in Sector 75, Noida. These developments represent a mix of office spaces, retail destinations, mixed-use SOHO formats and serviced apartments, reflecting the changing nature of commercial real estate demand across Noida and the wider NCR market. From an advisory perspective, commercial opportunities are evaluated on factors including location, connectivity, project status, developer credentials, surrounding development, market demand and leasing potential. Evolving commercial corridors create new opportunities Noida's commercial growth is increasingly extending beyond its established business districts. Infrastructure-led development along major expressways and connecting corridors is creating opportunities for new office, retail, hospitality and mixed-use destinations. From an investment perspective, infrastructure can play an important role in shaping the long-term potential of a real estate market. Improved connectivity, employment generation, commercial activity and supporting social infrastructure can collectively influence the attractiveness of emerging locations. The increasing integration of commercial developments with retail, hospitality, entertainment and lifestyle offerings is also creating more comprehensive business destinations rather than standalone office or retail clusters. As businesses continue to evaluate locations based on connectivity, accessibility and operational efficiency, commercial corridors with strong infrastructure linkages are likely to remain areas of interest. Looking ahead Noida's next phase of commercial growth is being shaped by the convergence of infrastructure development, corporate expansion and regional connectivity. The operationalisation of Noida International Airport represents a significant addition to the region's infrastructure network, while its developing passenger and cargo ecosystem could support further economic activity across Noida, Greater Noida and the Yamuna Expressway corridor. At the same time, the latest 2026 data from CBRE and Colliers points to continued demand for quality office space across India and Delhi-NCR. The record 66.4 million sq. ft. of office absorption across India during January-September 2026 and 8.3 million sq. ft. of Grade A leasing in Delhi-NCR during the same period reflect continued occupier activity. For investors and occupiers, the evolving market reinforces the importance of evaluating individual projects on fundamentals rather than relying solely on broader market trends. Factors such as location, connectivity, surrounding development, tenant or consumer demand, developer credentials, project status and the potential evolution of the micro-market remain important considerations. With infrastructure, connectivity and business activity continuing to develop, Noida is positioned to remain an important commercial destination within the wider Delhi-NCR economic ecosystem.
